firstMessage.rawMarkdown:
Sharing the code and results behind our paper-track submission, in case it saves others time. Everything was run in the official harness, unmodified, on the public tasks with verified reference patches.

1. vLLM's gemma4 parser drops edit_file calls that contain quotes. It splits a string argument at an inner " or a backtick, so old_string or new_string arrives missing and the call is rejected (vLLM issue 39069). In our first runs this dropped 34 of 60 edits. Three prompt rules brought it down to 1:
- write the edit strings as literal text;
- on that error, anchor the edit on nearby lines that contain no quotes;
- or apply the change with a python3 heredoc.

The exact wording is in prompts/measured_rules.md in the repo.

2. If you fine-tune a LoRA, check that <|tool_response> is supervised. Gemma 4 ends a tool-call turn by predicting that token, but in a rendered trajectory it opens the tool-result block. A mask that trains only model turns therefore never teaches the model to stop. Our adapter emitted up to 488 tool calls in one turn and fell from 17 to 8 solved out of 42, while the training loss looked normal.
- Fixing only the mask recovered most of the loss.
- Unsloth's response-only mask supervises the stop token but also trains on all tool output.
- transformers' assistant-tokens mask, which TRL's assistant-only loss relies on, supervises nothing on the Gemma 4 template.

analysis/check_stop_supervision.py checks any collator's output.

3. Most unsolved public tasks are missing information, not effort. Tasks whose statement is only a PR title were solved 11% of the time; adding the linked issue body raised that to 44%. Rules telling the agent to reproduce the bug, or to read the tests first, changed nothing. Neither did adding a locating stage, a code-briefing script, or a second reviewer agent: each landed at 25–26 of 64 against 27 for the plain agent.

4. Don't tune limits on the public tasks alone. The public tasks come from repositories the model has likely seen, so changes that look neutral there can matter on the hidden set. Cutting thinking and time budgets cost us nothing on the public tasks but did on the leaderboard. Treat the public tasks as a regression check rather than a predictor.

📝 Paper: https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/gemma-4-developer-agent-paper/writeups/new-writeup-1794490045534
💻 Code, mask checker and per-task results (Apache 2.0): https://github.com/shawnbaako/gemma4-agent-failure-analysis

The repo has no task text, patches or reference tests. Full agent configurations will follow after the final deadline.
